products.name: External Attack Surface Management (EASM)
products.description: Continuously indexes deep, dark, and surface web to map an organization's external digital footprint, shadow IT, exposed services and misconfigurations.

products.name: Continuous Automated Red Teaming (CART)
products.description: Patented (USPTO) system that discovers attack surface, identifies attack frontiers, prioritizes and emulates multi-stage attacks, determines attack paths, and continuously learns to generate an AI-based security model.

products.name: Agentic AI Penetration Testing (Web/API/Infrastructure)
products.description: AI agents autonomously discover assets, exploit vulnerabilities with proof-of-exploit validation, and chain findings into multi-stage attack paths (credential reuse, privilege escalation, lateral movement).

products.name: FireCompass Explorer
products.description: Freemium, credit-based self-serve product giving security teams immediate access to AI-powered autonomous pen testing for infrastructure, web apps, and APIs, launched Feb 5, 2026.

products.name: Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM)
products.description: Unifies exposure discovery, validation, and prioritization on a continuous cadence rather than point-in-time assessment.

products.name: Ransomware Attack Surface Testing (RAST)
products.description: Named as one of three core capability pillars (with EASM and CART) in partner announcements; not independently detailed by outside sources.

features.name: Zero-knowledge/autonomous asset discovery
features.description: Discovers external assets and shadow IT without requiring manual scoping.
features.how_it_works: Automated reconnaissance techniques described as mimicking nation-state-actor recon methods across deep, dark, and surface web.

features.name: Proof-of-exploit validation
features.description: Runs the actual exploit to prove a finding is real rather than relying on signature/heuristic matching, aiming for near-zero false positives.
features.how_it_works: Combines frontier large language models with FireCompass's own purpose-built small language models (SLMs) plus thousands of pre-built attack playbooks.

features.name: Multi-stage attack chaining
features.description: Chains individual findings (e.g., a web app vulnerability) into multi-stage attack paths reaching internal network footholds.
features.how_it_works: Reinforcement learning plus AI/ML subsystems that emulate attacker behavior across stages: discovery, frontier identification, prioritization, path determination, continuous learning (per USPTO patent description).

features.name: Credit-based freemium access (Explorer)
features.description: Lowers barrier to entry versus traditional weeks-long procurement/pilot cycles.
features.how_it_works: $2,000 in one-time free credits for self-serve use; $5,000-$10,000 in credits for white-glove enterprise pilots.

pricing: unverified - no official public price list found; third-party aggregator estimates cite a range of roughly $450-$2,500 per application for automated penetration testing on a subscription model, with tiers driven by number of assets/services monitored; Explorer freemium tier launched Feb 2026 uses a credit system ($2,000 free; $5,000-$10,000 for enterprise pilots)

research_highlights.title: FireCompass AI Agent Reaches Top 3 on HackerOne, Signalling a New Era of AI-Driven Cybersecurity for Enterprises
research_highlights.summary: Three-month live experiment (Apr-Jun 2026) running FireCompass AI agents on authorized HackerOne bug bounty programs with a $5,000/month budget, reaching top-3 leaderboard positions in several categories.

research_highlights.title: AI Pentest Agent Reaches HackerOne's Top 3 on a $5,000-a-Month Budget
research_highlights.summary: Republished coverage detailing methodology, safety controls (scope enforcement, non-destructive validation, rate/blast-radius limits), and submission statistics from the HackerOne experiment.

research_highlights.title: FireCompass Secures USPTO Patent for Continuous Automated Red Teaming (CART)
research_highlights.date: unverified exact date (patent grant referenced circa 2023-2024)
